notes:
Lead: Liam O'Connor. Sector: global shipping + logistics; heavy emphasis on vessel/off-network operation. Short summary: Atlas runs logistics and crew-support systems on multi-national vessels; they require a Private VPC deployment with an on-prem / air-gapped variant to run inference locally on ships and shore data centers.

Discovery highlights:
- Initial intro call 2024-09-12 (Liam + Priya + Atlas IT) — high-level interest in Private + Dedicated for shipboard workloads.
- Security questionnaire returned 2024-10-01; flagged KMS/HSM and FIPS questions.
- Fireflies call ff_20241002_AtlMar_ship-pilot-1 captured operational constraints: intermittent connectivity, signed software bundles only, no persistent outbound connections from ship network.
- POC ask: deploy a single-model on a 1U GPU appliance on vessel; offline bundle updates via signed artifacts; audit logs exported to on-prem ELK when connectivity available.

Technical requirements (customer paraphrase):
- "We can't have persistent tunnels to public endpoints from the ship — any agent must be fully air-gapped unless explicitly opened."
- KMS: integrate with onboard HSM (Yubico/HSMs) for key material; support for both remote KMS in shore DC and local HSM fallback.
- Audit logs: immutable audit trail stored shipboard for 7 years; regular push to shore once per week.
- Data residency: payloads originating in EU/UK flagged for regional retention; shore DC in Rotterdam preferred.
- Models: prefer smaller quantized variants for low-power inference; open to Redwood-verified quantized LLMs; want ability to pin model versions and fall back to lightweight rerankers when capacity constrained.
- Latency/Throughput: interactive crew assistant target <=200ms local token latency; throughput target 15-25 concurrent sessions per vessel.

Commercial/Procurement notes:
- Procurement lead: Maria Kostov (maritime IT). Procurement cycle starts Nov 2024; legal wants redlines on data residency and indemnity around on-board operation.
- Estimated ARR band provided as a range; pilot budget approved under OPEX for FY24.

POC plan proposed by Redwood (from SE):
1) Security architecture workshop (2-3 weeks) — map KMS/HSM, network constraints, signed bundle tooling.
2) Shipboard pilot on 1 vessel (6 weeks) — test offline model update, audit log retention & replay, failover to local reranker.
3) Shore integration & handoff (2 weeks) — ingestion to shore ELK, long-term retention policy.

Open questions / Risks:
- How to meet 7-year immutable on-ship audit retention with limited storage — consider compressed binary logs + weekly shore sync.
- HSM driver compatibility and FIPS certification window. Need known-good HW list.
- Warranty/legal around remote support when vessel is in high seas (insurance/ops).
